one_line: four-person course study of hypertension and treatment across Stroke Belt tracts
skills: census-tract data merging and geospatial joins
multiple linear regression on area-level data
permutation testing of preregistered directional hypotheses
outlier rules for bounded, skewed measures
data: CDC PLACES census-tract estimates (hypertension, medication coverage, obesity, smoking, inactivity, short sleep, cholesterol)
American Community Survey 5-year estimates via Cornell PolicyMap
Mapping Inequality HOLC redlining grades (HRI2020), Chicago phase
county-level files on stroke prevalence, insurance, medical debt and food insecurity

decisions.chose: widening the analysis from one metro area to the Stroke Belt states
decisions.over: keeping the preregistered analysis in the Chicago tracts already assembled
decisions.because: the cleaned Chicago sample was a tiny fraction of US tracts, and the broader region gave the hypotheses statistical power in a place where the hypertension burden is documented
decisions.evidence: As we designed our hypotheses, we decided to take this as an opportunity to increase statistical power.

decisions.chose: medication coverage among adults already diagnosed as the treatment outcome
decisions.over: comparing recorded hypertension prevalence across neighborhoods
decisions.because: a low recorded prevalence can reflect less testing or worse record-keeping rather than less disease, while the diagnosed population has at least baseline access to care
decisions.evidence: it may very well be the case that a "lower prevalence" of high blood pressure actually just reflects lower access to testing in the first place

decisions.chose: an interquartile-range rule for flagging high-burden outlier tracts
decisions.because: tract percentages are bounded and right-skewed, so quartile-based thresholds do not assume normality and are not distorted by a few extreme tracts
decisions.evidence: we used an interquartile range (IQR)–based rule rather than z-scores to identify outliers

decisions.chose: leaving the collinear behavioral risk measures out of the H2 model
decisions.over: entering physical inactivity, smoking and short sleep as controls alongside obesity
decisions.because: they are multicollinear with obesity, the predictor of interest, and would mostly add noise
decisions.evidence: Therefore, we will not include these variables as predictors to "control" for; they would do little more than introduce noise when used in conjunction with obesity

broke.what: tract IDs kept losing their leading zero when read as numbers, which silently breaks joins to the geometry and covariate files for states whose FIPS code starts with a zero
broke.evidence: Pandas consistently misinterprets the type of this column because Alabama's FIPS code has a leading zero.

broke.what: the H1 model cell was committed in an erroring state because the medication column had been renamed, fixed in the 'correcting hypertension label' commit
broke.evidence: KeyError: "['High Blood Pressure Medication'] not in index"

broke.what: the source column name for the treatment measure implied a share of the whole tract population rather than of diagnosed adults, so it was renamed before analysis
broke.evidence: it seems to imply that the values represent the proportion of the *total* tract population taking antihypertensives

question: Within the Stroke Belt, is high blood pressure more common in tracts with more obesity, and are diagnosed adults less likely to be on medication in tracts with a larger Black population share?
rejected_line: Built the first version around Chicago tracts and HOLC redlining grades; too few tracts survived cleaning, so the team moved to Stroke Belt states and dropped the redlining layer.
